agent_priors_used: General prior: autonomous research agents exhibit path dependence and local-attractor behavior; an inherited next_question can be locally rational yet globally suboptimal. Used to run a cognitive reset before continuing the flagged lanes, not as SPIDER evidence.

General prior: a treatment cannot be shown to beat a comparator that is already at ceiling; benchmark dynamic range is a prerequisite, not a post-hoc discovery. Used to keep B2 ahead of any four-arm benchmark; SPIDER has now independently instantiated this failure twice.

General prior: repeatedly rediscovering the same missing prerequisite across separate lanes is an anti-pattern; repair it once at the substrate/runtime level. Used to keep B2/B3 in single owner lanes rather than re-encoding the absence into more measurement-invalid packets.

General prior: small CPU-quantized language models frequently cannot emit reliable structured actions for multi-step tool-use; endpoint capability must be validated against the actual task before an expensive multi-arm benchmark is funded. Used only to frame the Intel capability test, not as evidence about any specific model.

General prior: shipping verified code through a pinned promotion path (rather than copying experiment code) prevents drift between the audited carrier and the production kernel. Used to scope the Product objective.

General prior: within-episode/local scratch is cheap and can close observation-absent residual, whereas cross-episode persistence pays a write+staleness cost; the value of persistence should track genuine re-acquisition cost. Used as a prior to prefer substrates engineered for asymmetric discovery.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Alternatives considered. (a) External competitor/baseline reconnaissance: valuable in general, but the Scout already covers breadth and the audit names the endpoint capability question as the live blocker, so this is lower information per cycle. (b) First-party C-PRODUCT-ECON measurement (h(N), Cwrite, Cmiss): this is not Intel's lane -- Intel is 'not a generic internal metrology lane' -- and it is downstream of the shipped carrier. (c) PIVOT to C-CROSSSITE external prior art: the claim is blocked on the shipped carrier and true holdout, so external search cannot yet alter a live decision. The endpoint-capability determination is the one external question that gates an active program decision.

allocation.question: Under the same credential-free, CPU-quantized constraints, does supplying the task goal/schema in the system prompt (removing the underspecification the parent harness did not have) convert the step-0 reveal-click into a full multi-step click-then-answer completion for the largest obtainable credential-free models, and if not, what is the demonstrable capability ceiling for the minimal Web-agent task across ALL credential-free endpoints and local models actually available to the factory? Return an explicit close/re-scope recommendation so that readiness condition (3) is either satisfied by a proven same-model driver or the four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT benchmark is re-scoped off the credential-free path. Include a bounded external check of the published capability envelope for comparably sized local models.
allocation.rationale: This is readiness condition (3) and the audit's priority 3. Intel owns endpoint/data/baseline provisioning, and its last packet (EXP-INTEL-37982024058) was a bounded FALSIFIES: 3B/7B Qwen cleared constrained-decoding positive controls but failed the minimal Web-agent task 0/5 and 0/5 under an underspecified system prompt. Whether that is a model-capability ceiling or a prompt/underspecification artifact is a single bounded, decision-changing question: a positive result unlocks the four-arm benchmark; a negative result closes the credential-free path and forces an explicit re-scope. Leaving the lane idle would leave the flagship benchmark with no determination of its own linchpin.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: 433 canonical experiments; no claim has moved since the 2026-10-10 audit. Effective epistemic state: C-MEAS-VALID VALIDATED (bounded to the authorship-separated real-Chromium fixture scope); C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-FRESHNESS, C-DELTA-REPAIR and C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY EXPERIMENTAL; C-LLM-INHERIT, C-CROSSSITE, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, C-PRODUCT-ECON and C-WEB-DYNAMICS HYPOTHESIS. The program is no longer bottlenecked on missing science; it is bottlenecked on three readiness prerequisites on the single decisive causal chain (observe -> parameterized mechanism -> executable binding in the SHIPPED treatment -> applicability/freshness -> real external agent -> lower cost per successful partially novel task): B1 the shipped kernel still lacks the audited parameterized carrier (main exposes literal distill() at confidence 0.5, no distill_parameterized()); B2 the credential-free deterministic REST task class has zero dynamic range (cold and retrieval both saturate at 1.0 at high novelty, established twice by Product); B3 no credential-free endpoint/local model has yet cleared the minimal multi-step Web-agent capability bar (3B/7B Qwen failed the underspecified task). Strong bounded negatives are correctly retired rather than re-litigated: value-level persistence/predictability on the credential-free HTTP substrate (prevalence 0.0435), external f* reportability from the one hash-pinned artifact, and the four-arm benchmark as specified. This cycle therefore funds exactly the blocker-removal work and two pre-freeze threads whose outcomes change a decision, and it deliberately does NOT fund the expensive C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON execution, because readiness conditions (2) and (3) are still missing. Concentration warnings (graph and physics tunnel flags) were treated as diagnostic, not as quotas: in both cases the pending pre-freeze mandate is the globally correct next problem under the audit.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout ran in DEGRADED SCOUT MODE (model unavailable, rc=124): no external reconnaissance, `spider_evidence`, `external_directional_context` and `cross_lane_dependencies` were all empty, and its candidate directions were restatements of the pending pre-freeze mandates or of the lanes' own parent handoffs. It therefore could not and did not alter any allocation; I treated it as non-authoritative staff advice and reasoned from the machine snapshot, `codex/claim_state.json.effective_event_by_claim`, and the dated program audit. Where the Scout offered a discretionary alternative it was weighed and rejected on the merits: for Frontier it floated the recorded maintenance/invalidation economics thread as an alternative to the site-native-discovery question, but I chose the discovery question because it tests the load-bearing assumption of the current architecture synthesis (that Web depth makes state re-acquisition materially expensive), whereas the maintenance thread largely re-measures freshness economics already under Graph. For Graph, Physics, Runtime and Product the Scout's candidate directions coincide with the pre-freeze mandates I independently judged still correct, so no pivot was warranted. The Scout's advisory questions ('which blocker most constrains residual-novelty economics' and 'which lanes repeat measurement-repair whose prerequisite should be repaired once') were answered directly by the B1/B2/B3 allocation rather than by dispatching those lanes elsewhere.
